sources.entry: otter-browser - Otter Browser aims to recreate the best aspects of the classic Opera (12.x) UI using Qt5.

summary.one_liner: Otter Browser is a free, GPL v3 licensed desktop web browser, written in C++ on Qt, that aims to recreate the UI and power-user features of Opera 12.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Otter Browser as a browser meant to recreate the best aspects of Opera 12 and revive its spirit, with powerful features for power users while staying fast and lightweight. Planned features are tracked in a TODO file and implemented features are documented in a CHANGELOG file. It is built from source with CMake against Qt 5.15 or newer, using OpenSSL and GStreamer for multimedia. Pre-compiled binaries are offered as an AppImage for Linux, through distribution and BSD repositories, and as Windows binaries on SourceForge. The README also notes JavaScript is used to interact with rendering engines and Python 3 for development tools, and translations are handled through Transifex.
use_cases: Browsing the web on a desktop with an Opera 12 style interface
Using a lightweight, power-user focused browser on Linux, BSD or Windows
Building a browser from C++ source with Qt
notable: Aims to revive the Opera 12 user interface and spirit
Released under GNU GPL v3, with an explicit goal of user control
Linux AppImage needs no dependencies installed, per the README
Pre-built binaries for Linux, BSD and Windows as well as source builds
Community IRC channels on Libera.Chat and an official forum
caveats: Building from source requires Qt 5.15 or newer, OpenSSL and GStreamer with codecs, and CMake 3.16 or newer
The AppImage needs OpenSSL 1.0.x (not 1.1.x) and GStreamer 1.x on the host system, per the README
The README does not state a specific release status or maintenance level
